note: Window agent p1920-p1929, 2 Nov 2026. Fills the Rhodesia gap (the Company's losses went to nobody for 1923-1926), keeps Kufra with the Senussi, removes the Smyrna enclave from the Greek 1922 shape, keeps Vilnius Polish in the 1924 shapes.

union.text: Mashonaland in the wide sense, the Shona country east of the Ndebele realm: Fort Salisbury (Harare), Masvingo (Fort Victoria) and Manicaland
Matabeleland, 'Mzilikazi's settlement in what is now Matabeleland, Zimbabwe'
the former Rozvi heartland around Danamombe
Matabeleland and the Midlands: 'The kingdom was located between the Sanyati and Limpopo rivers'; the Rozvi state was 'conquered and subdued around 1838 by Mzilikazi's Ndebele'

region.text: Southern Rhodesia (Mashonaland and Matabeleland), the land the Company's charter administered until the Crown annexed it

events.note: 12 September 1923: the Crown annexes Southern Rhodesia ('the territory was annexed by the United Kingdom on 12 September 1923'); 'on 1 October 1923, the first constitution for the colony came into force'. The Company's loss event (counterpart southern-rhodesia, no dossier) sent the land to nobody until the 1926 British Africa keyframe; the colony is drawn as British Africa's land, as that keyframe does.

minus.text: the late-19th-century state: 'covered around 150,000 sq mi (390,000 km2)', with Lozi influence from the Kwito River in the west to the Kafue River in the east; drawn as a 352 km disc round Mongu, which has the page's 390,000 km2 area but not its two river limits

the Bulozi (Barotse) Floodplain of the Zambezi and surrounding territory: 'expanded to cover the Bulozi Floodplain and surrounding territories'; the Western Province of Zambia stands in for the floodplain
the Lozi realm outside Bulozi proper

union.text: the outer realm in Zambia and Botswana, outside Bulozi proper: the 1899 Order gave Lewanika's powers there to the British South Africa Company

region.text: Northern Rhodesia (Barotziland-North-Western and North-Eastern Rhodesia), the land the Company administered until 1 April 1924

events.note: 1 April 1924: 'On 1 April 1924, Herbert Stanley was appointed as Governor and Northern Rhodesia became an official Protectorate' of the United Kingdom, 'with its administrative machinery taken over by the Colonial Office'. The Company's loss event (counterpart northern-rhodesia, no dossier) left Zambia to nobody for 1924-1925 until the 1926 British Africa keyframe.

region.text: the Kufra district, the oases around Kufra, the Senussi stronghold until 1931

events.note: Under the 1920 Accord of al-Rajma Idris was 'permitted to administer autonomously the oases around Kufra'; Kufra was 'the last stronghold of the Senussi in Libya' until 'In 1931, Italian forces seized Kufra'. The page names no British or Egyptian land in Libya; the Cliopatria British Africa shape (kept by the British Africa keyframes of 1920, 1922 and 1926) draws 1,389 Kufra cells as British.

correction.text: the 1922 shape without Eastern Thrace (evacuated under the Armistice of Mudanya) and without the Smyrna enclave, which Cliopatria's 1922 shape still draws (14 cells round Izmir)

keyframe_overrides.why: 'The Turkish cavalry rode into the town around eleven o'clock on the Saturday morning of 9 September' 1922 and 'The expulsion of the Greek Army from Anatolia was completed on 18 September'; the Greek ledger ends the Smyrna occupation in September 1922, but the 1922 keyframe put 14 Izmir cells back as direct Greek land, which the 1924 keyframe (no Turkish cell) was too small a change to remove, so Greece kept Smyrna to 1930.

correction.text: the 1924 shape without Vilnius and its environs (about 6,880 km2), which Poland held from 1922 to 1939

keyframe_overrides.why: Central Lithuania 'was incorporated into Poland on 18 April 1922' and its land went into the Wilno Voivodeship while 'Lithuania declined to accept the Polish authority'; Vilnius 'and its surroundings' were given to Lithuania only in October 1939 (Mutual Assistance Treaty of 10 October 1939). Cliopatria's 1924 Lithuania shape draws Vilnius as Lithuanian, which handed it over in 1924.

correction.text: the 1924 shape plus Vilnius and its environs (about 6,880 km2), which Poland held from 1922 to October 1939

keyframe_overrides.why: Poland held Vilnius from the incorporation of Central Lithuania (18 April 1922) to October 1939; Cliopatria's 1924 Polish shape leaves the Vilnius area out, so the 1924 snap took Poland's Vilnius cells away.

rulings.why: Kufra was the Senussi's 'last stronghold in Libya' until the Italians seized it in 1931 (Idris administered 'the oases around Kufra' under the 1920 Accord of al-Rajma); the page gives Britain and Egypt no land in Libya. The size rule gives the colony (R1) the cells at each British Africa keyframe (1920, 1922, 1926, 1927, 1930); the ruling keeps them with the Senussi.
